statement: Modular engine cylinder, fluid radiator, heat exchanger, air scoop, wing section, control surface, control fin, diesel engine, jet exhaust, jet combustion chamber, PID controller, powered joint, advanced radar, legacy radar and sonar, radio and propeller, rotor and ducted fan articles (and their component pages) have an "Interactive graphs" section. `components/FormulaSection.jsx` renders the formula as MathML, the assumptions and the cited executable constants on the server. `components/FormulaGraphs.jsx` is the client chart: native sliders, a select and checkboxes drive an SVG plot, a persistent selected-point readout and a data table, all server-rendered in their default state. The formulas live in `lib/formulas.js`, and `graphKindsForFamily` decides which families get a graph. The jet exhaust graph plots force in internal units against the exhaust's incoming pressure, with altitude, Thrust Spoiler, afterburner and stored-fuel inputs and an optional 100 × S application cap for an example scale S. It does not plot force against RPS, because the pressure an assembled engine reaches depends on its duct network, which was not reconstructed. The combustion chamber graph plots jet fuel L/s and the pressure and temperature added per update against RPS and throttle. The joint graph plots speed and holding cap against the six Gear Ratio options, relative to 1:1, for every powered pivot, hinge, turret ring, piston and track. The modular engine cylinder graph has two plots: the efficiency factors against crank speed, and crank RPS over simulated time from `modularEngineResponse`, a port of `investigation/native/modular-engines/tools/engine_step.py` for a chosen cylinder count and size, crankshafts, flywheel, fuel throttle, air:fuel ratio and an optional clutch to an output held at a fixed speed. The advanced radar graph plots the farthest distance at which a target passes the radar's score test against the target's physics-body mass (game mass units, log scale), with the radar and both FOV axes over the editor's 0.01 to 0.25 range as inputs; it levels off at the working range R from mass 250. The legacy radar and sonar graph plots the farthest on-axis passing distance, min(C, 4 × S), against the same mass for the six type-16 sensors, with the far plane C at the saved radar_fov default 0.1. The propeller graph, a port of `investigation/native/propulsion/tools/model.py` checked bit for bit against its worked examples, plots raw internal force (before the 100 × S cap) or RPS removed per update against published shaft RPS for any of the 23 force-emitter parts, with effective pitch, relative flow U and a hub-under-water toggle as inputs. Air parts draw two lines, one per candidate solver weight, because the selector byte between them is an open question.

The result is in the game's internal force units. Body mass is not calibrated to kilograms, so do not read it as newtons. The game queues the force once per update and the physics solver integrates it, so it is not multiplied by 60. Before it is applied its size is limited to 5 × S, where S is a per-vehicle scale passed in by the component dispatcher; area scaling is linear only below that limit.

Partly under water, the air force is scaled by 1 minus the immersion fraction and a separate water term takes over.

The force equations come from static decompilation of one build; the game was not run. How the game builds the cap scale S for craft joined by locked joints was not decoded, so forces near the cap are not predicted.

Exhaust force = 32 × (incoming pressure - 1000) × altitude factor × afterburner multiplier × (1 - Thrust Spoiler), before a cap of 100 × S, with S a per-vehicle scale. RPS enters only through the pressure the chamber adds, so the tooltip's proportionality to internal RPS describes the chain, not the exhaust formula. The altitude factor 1 - height × 1.5 ÷ 40000 reaches 0 at a height of 26666.67, metres if the height field is in metres, which is an inference. The three exhausts use the same coefficient; the rotating one only changes direction.

Physical units of jet pressure and temperature were not established; pressure, temperature, charge and force stay in internal units. How the game builds the cap scale S for craft joined by locked joints was not decoded, so forces near the cap are not predicted.

Propellers, rotors and ducted fans share one force-emitter update. Shaft speed and normalized pitch set a load that takes speed off the shaft and turns it into internal force T = 1500 × K × removed RPS × efficiency. force_emitter_max_force sets the solver weight K, not a thrust ceiling, and a separate 100 × S cap limits the applied force. Marine parts push only with the hub underwater, air parts only above it.

Not decoded: which loaded value sets the air weight selector byte (+0x580 behind the definition's first pointer) for each air part, so air figures stay in two branches; the full source of the cap scale S and the SI calibration of force, torque and shaft power; the visible cyclic blade phase; the separate water-interaction helper 0x1402fe950, cavitation and other hydrodynamics outside the scalar law; whether anything elsewhere in the engine adds ground effect (the scalar law has no ground-clearance term); the editor-arrow sign table for reflected parts. No figure here was measured in a running game.

The small boat propeller receives engine power and its tooltip says it operates only underwater. The controllable-pitch boat propeller also requires underwater operation and takes desired pitch from -1 to 1. Its force_emitter_max_force field is 80000 versus 20000 for the selected small fixed-pitch propeller. A native decode (investigation/propulsion.md, shown on the Propulsion parts pages) found that every propeller, rotor and ducted fan runs one force-emitter update. Each update it scales the published shaft speed by 0.9999 to w, forms the effective pitch p = clamp(saved pitch + Pitch input, -1, 1) and the load b = (2 × w × rotation_speed × π × blade_physics_length × p × 0.75 + p × U) × blade_efficiency × intact blades × 0.32, where U is minus the hub's velocity through still water along the thrust axis, signed by the pitch. With K = force_emitter_max_force ÷ 1000, or F × intact blades ÷ 8000 for the pitchable propellers, q = clamp(b ÷ 2K, -10, 10) is multiplied by 10 below the water surface; the propeller removes w × (1 - 1 ÷ (1 + q²)) RPS from its shaft and pushes with 1500 × K × removed RPS, signed by the pitch, in the game's internal force unit. Thrust is queued only when the hub is at or below the sampled water surface; the shaft load applies either way. force_emitter_max_force is therefore a solver weight, not a thrust ceiling: at 10 RPS and pitch 1 the small fixed propeller gives about 22201 internal force, and the small, standard and large pitchable propellers about 4074, 20411 and 35002 per RPS. Pitch is a normalized number, not a blade angle; zero pitch gives no load and no thrust. A separate application cap of 100 × S limits the force actually applied.

The propeller law comes from that native decode, not from these fields alone.
